latin.587: GAR. 4. At sic argumentantur, eos memores esse oportebat eorum quae prius dixerunt. Si peccatum Adami accipiatur non pro actione ipsa praecise sumpta, sed simul cum corruptione quam peperit, recte dici Adami peccatum posteris imputari. Nam ita peccatum erit, & ipsa Adami actio & corruptio consequens.
latin.588: Itaque ut recte dicimur peccare in Adamo propter corruptionem in nobis ab Adamo descendentem: Ita & vere peccare dicemur in eo, propter actionem quam Adamus praecessit.
latin.589: PLAC. Quomodo id antea fuerit dictum, & quantum faveat imputationi antecedenti, satis patere arbitramur ex dictis supra pag. 151. 152. 153. Quorsum igitur pertineat, & quam vim habeat haec Viri docti responsio, non intelligo.
latin.590: Certe corruptio nostra est, quia in nos propagata, intra nos est; actio vero quae corruptionem peperit non est nostra nisi quatenus corruptio eius quaedam participatio, & in eam consensio est.
latin.591: GAR. 5. Negatur illud, cui totam suam rationem superstruit Vir doctus, Qui peccarunt, ita ut iustam condemnationem meriti sint, eos vere & proprie peccasse. Quid si vere & proprie peccare est in propria sua persona peccare, & suo non alieno peccato delinquere? Proprium enim alieno opponitur.
latin.592: At etiam qui alieno peccato peccant, id est, quibus alienum peccatum imputatur, & iustam condemnationem merentur. Nam filii Saulis peccaverunt alieno, nempe patris, peccato, & tamen iustam mortis condemnationem ex Dei mandato perpessi sunt, adeoque meruerunt, quia iusta sunt Dei iudicia. Et peccata, quibus patres actu peccarunt, non sunt proprie peccata filiorum, quia non sunt ab iis personaliter patrata; & tamen iuxta Decalogi comminationem, propter ea filii in varias poenas & iustam condemnationem incurrunt. Ita ergo possumus in Adamo peccasse, ut iustam mortis sententiam meriti simus, & tamen non ideo huc deveniendum est ut dicamus nos proprie sive personaliter peccasse, cum Adamus peccavit; sed tantum ita censeri apud Deum, ac si cum ipse peccavit omnes peccassemus.

pass_a.587: GAR's fourth move: recall the earlier reading. Take Adam's sin not as the bare act alone, but with the corruption it produced—then it is rightly imputed to the posterity, for both act and following corruption are the sin.
pass_a.588: On his pairing: the vice that flows down from Adam into us already grounds 'sinning in him,' and he adds the same for Adam's earlier deed itself—so both the inherited spoil and the paradise act are made to underwrite the phrase.
pass_a.589: Placeus: how that helps antecedent imputation is already on pp. 151–153. Where this reply points, and what force it has, I do not see.
pass_a.590: Placeus grants the spoil is ours once it lives inside us by generation. He refuses to treat the begetting deed as ours in the same way: it becomes ours only as that spoil is a share in it and a yes to it—not as a personal repeat of paradise.
pass_a.591: GAR 5 denies the hinge Placeus used: that meriting just condemnation means one truly and properly sinned. Properly may mean only in one's own person, by one's own—not another's—sin.
pass_a.592: Yet even those who sin by another's sin—that is, to whom another's sin is imputed—also merit just condemnation. Saul's sons sinned by the father's sin and still suffered just death by God's command, for his judgments are just. The fathers' actual sins are not properly the sons' personally, yet under the Decalogue's threat the sons incur penalties for them. So we can have sinned in Adam so as to merit death without saying we personally sinned when he did; only that God reckons us as if, when he sinned, we all had. Tip before Placeus takes up vere/falso and proprie.

587: GAR. 4. But so they argue: they ought to have been mindful of those things which they said before. If Adam's sin is taken not for the act itself precisely taken, but together with the corruption which it begot, Adam's sin is rightly said to be imputed to the posterity. For so it will be sin, both Adam's act itself and the following corruption.
588: And so as we are rightly said to sin in Adam because of the corruption descending into us from Adam: so also we shall be said truly to sin in him, because of the act which Adam performed before.
589: PLAC. How that was said before, and how much it favors antecedent imputation, we judge to appear sufficiently from what was said above at pages 151, 152, 153. Whither therefore this reply of the learned man pertains, and what force it has, I do not understand.
590: Certainly the corruption is ours, because propagated into us, it is within us; but the act which begot the corruption is not ours except insofar as the corruption is a certain participation of it, and there is consent unto it.
591: GAR. 5. That is denied on which the learned man builds his whole reason, that those who have so sinned that they have merited just condemnation have truly and properly sinned. What if to sin truly and properly is to sin in one's own person, and to offend by one's own, not by another's, sin? For one's own is opposed to another's.
592: And yet even those who sin by another's sin, that is, to whom another's sin is imputed, also merit just condemnation. For Saul's sons sinned by another's, namely the father's, sin, and yet they suffered the just condemnation of death by God's command, and so merited it, because God's judgments are just. And the sins by which the fathers actually sinned are not properly the sons' sins, because they were not personally committed by them; and yet according to the Decalogue's threat, because of them the sons incur various penalties and just condemnation. So therefore we can have sinned in Adam so as to have merited the just sentence of death, and yet we need not for that reason come to this, that we say we properly or personally sinned when Adam sinned; but only that we are so reckoned before God, as if when he himself sinned all of us had sinned.
